{!Contact.FirstName},
Thank you for your interest in the Professional Science Master's (PSM) in Nanoscience degree program at Arizona State University. We offer the following three program options:
Nano-Materials and Nanoscale Devices Biophysics and Biomedical Technology Biochemistry and Sensing Technology
Feel free to contact individual faculty members to discuss research possibilities and assistantships. A list of the faculty can be found here.
We are now accepting applications to our PSM in Nanoscience program for the 2016-2017 academic year. For program details, please visit our site. We offer rolling admission by conducting on-going application reviews. To receive full consideration, an application must be submitted along with all the required supplemental documents. Details on the application process can be found here, along with instructions on how to submit hard copies of transcripts and GRE/TOEFL scores.
The PSM program is targeted at both recent graduates and, especially, working professionals who wish to retrain into nanoscience, nanotechnology, and related areas. commercial innovation is particularly emphasized throughout the program, including applications into optics, semiconductor electronics and optoelectronics, sensors, nanomedicine, and health care. Since this program is unique, it is registered with the WRGP (Western Region Graduate Program) which allows students from most western states to pay fees at in-state tuition rates.
The PSM program consists of 30 credits to be completed on an accelerated 12-month track or a part-time 24-month track. This immersive learning experience does not require a thesis and takes place in a research-intensive, professional atmosphere. Core courses (15 credits - including an applied project) are designed to help PSM students improve their knowledge in a range of subjects. These include courses in innovation and IP management and in nanoscience and society. The remaining 15 credits are electives selected by the participant from the program options listed above. Throughout the program, students engage with faculty and peers to learn through discussion on topics related to nanoscience. Visiting speakers and industry professionals enhance the program through their involvement in the two-semester long Professional Seminar.
Applicants must hold a bachelor's or master's degree in physics, chemistry, or a related field (such as Materials Science or Electrical Engineering) from a regionally accredited institution. Applications must be submitted online accompanied by official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate course work, a statement of purpose, and two letters of recommendation from individuals aware of the applicant's potential. GRE scores are not required, but will be taken into consideration if submitted. TOEFL (or equivalent) score for non-native English speakers will be required when applicable.
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Ms. Ixchell Paape (Physics Specialist) by phone at 480-965-0355 or by email at Ixchell.Paape@asu.edu.
Sincerely,
Dr. John Venables Professor of Physics Director of the PSM in Nanoscience Program Department of Physics Arizona State University
